newsitem.title: ITALY: Famous Rome fountain damaged by diving bathers.
newsitem.headline: Famous Rome fountain damaged by diving bathers.

text.p: A famous fountain in Rome's elegant Piazza Navona was damaged on Tuesday when three men took a dip to escape the summer heat and used part of it as a diving board, witnesses said.
A metre-long (three feet) piece from the tail of a dragon in the stone 17th century baroque masterpiece carved by Gian Lorenzo Bernini snapped off when the men dived from it.
The three men, all from Rome, were arrested, said a police spokesman who did not name them.
One of the men told the police he had leapt into the water to try to cool down as temperatures in the Italian capital soared over 30 degrees Celsius (86 Fahrenheit).
The broken tail was retrieved in three pieces from the bottom of the fountain basin by an Irish tourist.
The fountain, named the "Four Rivers", represents four continents with personifications of the Nile, Danube, Ganges and Rio Plate rivers.
